# Solar Watts to Recharge a 1,000Wh Power Station

**About 300–400W of panels refills a 1,000Wh station in one sunny day. About 200W takes roughly a day and a half.**

## The formula

**Panel watts ≈ battery Wh ÷ (peak sun hours × 0.75)**

The 0.75 accounts for real-world losses from heat, panel angle and the charge controller. Panels usually deliver only 60–85% of their rated watts. ([enoughwatts.com](https://enoughwatts.com/guides/how-much-solar-to-recharge), [powerpreflight.com](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/))

Peak sun hours are not the same as daylight hours. One peak sun hour equals an hour of full-strength sun.

## Panel watts for a full recharge in one day

| Peak sun hours | Panel watts needed |
|---|---|
| 3 (cloudy or winter) | ~450W |
| 4 | ~340W |
| 5 | ~270W |
| 6 (Southwest or summer) | ~230W |

Source: [power-runtime.pages.dev](https://power-runtime.pages.dev/guides/solar-charging/)

Most of the US averages about 4.5 peak sun hours, ranging from about 3.8 in Seattle to 6.6 in Phoenix ([watt48.com](https://www.watt48.com/guides/solar-panel-charging-power-station)). In a northern winter, a one-day recharge can take 700W or more ([heldinreserve.com](https://www.heldinreserve.com/power/solar-panels-recharge-power-station/)).

**Rule of thumb:** divide the battery's Wh by 5. For a 1,000Wh station, that's about 200W, which recharges it in roughly 1.5 days of decent sun ([powerpreflight.com](https://powerpreflight.com/guides/solar-panel-sizing-portable-power-stations/)).

## Check your station's specs before buying

1. **Maximum solar input (watts).** Panel watts above this cap add nothing. Some stations cap at 200W, and with that cap a 1,000Wh station takes about 1.5 days no matter how many panels you connect.
2. **Input voltage range.** The panel's open-circuit voltage (Voc) must stay inside the station's range. Exceeding it can damage the charge controller.
3. **Connector.** Panels usually use MC4 plugs. Stations use XT60, DC barrel or proprietary ports, so make sure you have the right adapter.

These figures assume you aren't running anything off the station while it charges. Any load slows the recharge.

## Example panel

The **ALLPOWERS SP037 400W foldable panel** would refill a 1,000Wh station in about a day of average sun, if your station accepts 400W.
- Price: $299, or $269.10 with code **ALLPOWERS26** (10% off). Dealectric reports the code was tested on 2026-10-21 and expires 2026-12-30.
- Voc is 45.3V, so your station needs to accept roughly 12–60V. It's too high for 12–28V inputs.
- It's heavy for a folding panel at 18.5 kg (about 41 lb).
- [Buy the ALLPOWERS SP037](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel). This is an affiliate link that goes to ALLPOWERS's US store. ([details](https://dealectric.com/allpowers-sp037-400w-solar-panel))
